reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling (NVA4) in northern Virginia publishes 11 MW of IT load capacity, representing roughly 275 racks or approximately 2,200 accelerators at typical AI training density, a modest single-facility footprint below the scale where infrastructure becomes a binding constraint on large-scale model training.

Sterling ranks 22nd among Virginia's 25 facilities with published capacity figures, holding 0.7% of the state's total. Virginia maps 330 data center locations but only 25 disclose power specifications, indicating most of the state's infrastructure capacity remains undisclosed. Within the published set, Sterling occupies a mid-tier position by power consumption.

The facility lists 128,715 square feet of technical space and carries no certifications, a profile consistent with a regional colocation operation serving enterprise and cloud tenants rather than hyperscale AI training. Sterling's individual contribution to AI compute scaling is minor compared to the largest regional operators, and the broader pattern of undisclosed capacity in Virginia suggests that published figures capture only a fraction of actual data center infrastructure in the state.
